finding.claim: The /rss route passes the unvalidated query parameter u directly to URI.open, so an unauthenticated caller can make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal or metadata URLs and read the first 400 bytes of the response.

trace.note: params[:u] is read from the request and passed directly to URI.open
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched body to the caller, so the response is not blind

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist on the /rss path; TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is defined but unused here. No scheme restriction. No authentication visible in app.rb. open-uri follows redirects by default and nothing re-validates the redirect target. Severity HIGH.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /rss route (app.rb:7-10) has no allowlist, scheme check, or auth. TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is only used by /trusted (app.rb:14), not /rss. No before-filter or middleware is defined in app.rb.
verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] straight into URI.open(...).read with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns data[0, 400] to the caller, so an unauthenticated query parameter reaches an outbound fetch whose response is returned to the requester.

finding.claim: Closed: the /trusted route enforces strict parsed-host set membership before the request, and Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. Residual, not SSRF: scheme and port are unrestricted, so only the two trusted hosts on arbitrary ports are reachable.

trace.note: TRUSTED.include?(uri.host) strict set membership, halts with 400 otherwise
Net::HTTP.get(uri) issues the request only after the check passes

finding.guards_checked: Strict set membership on uri.host (userinfo and suffix tricks rejected). Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. Scheme and port are not restricted (hardening only).

verdict.guard_found: app.rb:14 `halt 400, "no" unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host)`, where TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is the exact two-hostname set. This is exact membership on the parsed host, which is a closing guard. app.rb:15 `Net::HTTP.get(uri)` is reached only after it passes.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.rb:13-15 and the source `params[:u]` is attacker-controlled, but the exact parsed-host set check at app.rb:14 closes the SSRF path, so the only remaining issue is hardening (unrestricted scheme and port), not SSRF.

finding.claim: Closed: /version fetches a hardcoded GitHub API URL with no user input.
finding.guards_checked: No user-controlled value reaches the sink.

verdict.guard_found: none; no guard is needed because no user-controlled value reaches the sink. app.rb:19 passes only a string literal to URI() and Net::HTTP.get, and the handler at app.rb:18-20 reads no params.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: app.rb:19 builds Net::HTTP.get(URI("https://api.github.com/repos/example/example/releases/latest")) from a literal with no params access, so there is no attacker-controlled source and no SSRF, which means the "closed" status is correct and the SSRF finding is refuted.
